security_problem: The identity-aware path is proven to deny inside the decision path and never proven at the backend. Six tests in internal/proxy/verified_actor_test.go assert that the proxy returned a denial; none of them proves the MCP server never received the call. H50's own text admits the limit: deny-before-relay at the intercept gate, not host/network isolation or an independent backend observer. A denial returned to the client for a call that was already relayed would satisfy every existing test and still be a complete failure of the property the project claims.
required_behavior: One canonical harness entry point (harness/identity-aware.sh, which runs tests/integration/verified_actor_harness_test.go with -count=1 -v) starts a mock MCP backend and a visor serve process configured with settings.require_verified_actor, drives the positive and negative scenario tables of the design contract, and asserts the exit criterion server_received(action) IMPLIES verified_actor(action) AND policy_allowed(action) AND durable_allow(action) from the backend observer's own artifact. The observer is a mock backend that appends one JSON line per received tools/call, recording received_at, transaction, method, tool and a hash of the raw argument bytes exactly as received on the wire (no decode/re-marshal), to a file it owns outside the repository (a temp directory), and it must not import internal/audit or read visor's ledger: its only inputs are the bytes it receives on the wire. The observer creates one exclusive session file and writes a `start` record, one record per received `tools/call`, and an `end` record only after stdin reaches end-of-stream; every write is length-checked and fsynced, a write/sync/parse failure writes an `observer_error` record and never `end`, and the terminal record is also delivered as one atomic line on a completion FIFO. Runtime scenarios send a non-`tools/call` barrier request and read its client response before SIGKILLing the proxy, then wait on the FIFO with a bounded deadline and only afterwards read the artifact. For every negative scenario the test asserts observer_received == false from that completed session, correlated by transaction id and never by ordering or by emptiness, through one receipt helper that returns received or not-received only after authenticating the session and fails the test as UNKNOWN on every other outcome (missing or non-`end` terminal record, unreadable artifact, missing `start`, prefix digest or count mismatch, `observer_error`, duplicate or unexpected transaction id); the client stream is a test-owned pipe and carries exactly one JSON-RPC response for each id the test sent; for at least one positive scenario it asserts the artifact exists and is non-empty, so a missing artifact fails the test rather than passing it by omission. A discriminating control proves the negatives come from the gate: with settings.require_verified_actor absent, the same call carries no context and the observer receives it. harness/identity-aware.sh points the observer at a run-unique directory under evidence/harness/<timestamp>/ (an excluded evidence tree, so the recorded snapshot digest is unchanged by the run), so no two runs share an artifact file and the repository never receives the observer log at any other path. harness/invariants.md gains one new row mapping each H52 property to the exact test that proves it and to the observer artifact field that proves it; the H50 row is not edited, widened or re-scoped.
failure_behavior: Every negative scenario fails the test if the observer recorded the call, if the denial is not produced, or if the artifact cannot be read; a missing or unreadable observer artifact is a failure, never a pass by omission. An observer session that cannot be proven complete — no terminal record within the deadline, no `end` record, a digest, byte-count or call-count mismatch, an `observer_error` record, a duplicate record, a record for a transaction the scenario never sent, or a missing barrier response — fails the test as UNKNOWN and never counts as 'the backend received nothing'. If the observer dies, a record write or sync fails, the run is killed, or the wait times out, the scenario fails. A runtime scenario never closes the proxy's stdin and never sends it a signal, so the proxy's own shutdown path (which closes the backend's input and then kills it) is never used. A scenario that cannot distinguish a gate denial from an unrelated failure fails the test, because the discriminating control must forward the same call when the identity requirement is absent. harness/identity-aware.sh exits non-zero when the test fails and does not write the artifact anywhere inside the digest-tracked tree.
non_goals: No enforcement change: this adds proof, it does not change the gate, its decisions or its reasons
Do not edit, widen, weaken or re-scope H50 or any existing invariant row
No compose stack, network topology or direct-bypass tests (separate card)
No evidence-correlation work across stable shared IDs (separate card)
No new capability-token format, no new policy schema, no new CLI flag for the proxy
No LLM, scoring, or model-generated claim anywhere in the decision or verification path
No host filesystem or network confinement
No dashboard or web control plane
No merge of mcp-visor with the identity-plane repository
